## Overview

A categorical specification can be *lowered* to many different concrete
realizations. Earlier vignettes lowered nets to matrix projection models,
integral projection models, continuous-time generators, and their
demographic-stochastic variants. This vignette adds the final route: an
**individual-based model** (IBM) on the
[Ark.jl](https://github.com/ark-ecs/Ark.jl) entity-component-system,
provided by `IndividualBasedPopulationDynamics.jl`.

The same `ValuedProjectionNet` and the same `fecundity` tagging that drive
the deterministic and demographic lowerings also drive the IBM lowering —
so one specification yields a deterministic mean, a continuous-time
Markov chain, *and* a population of simulated individuals.

## Setup

```{julia}
using CategoricalPopulationDynamics
using IndividualBasedPopulationDynamics: ibm_run_stage!
using Random, LinearAlgebra, Plots
```

## A stage-structured valued net

Three stages — juvenile, sub-adult, adult — with maturation transitions
and adult reproduction:

```{julia}
vnet = ValuedProjectionNet([:juv, :sub, :adult],
    :maturation   => [(:juv => :sub) => 0.5, (:sub => :adult) => 0.4],
    :reproduction => [(:adult => :juv) => 0.6])
stage_names(vnet), transition_names(vnet)
```

The move-vs-birth split (shared with the demographic targets) is what the
lowering uses: `:reproduction` is tagged as fecundity (births), the rest
are inter-stage movements.

```{julia}
U, F = survival_fecundity_matrices(vnet; fecundity = [:reproduction])
(movements = U, births = F)
```

## Lowering to an individual-based model

`IBMStageTarget` carries the initial per-stage counts, the fecundity tag,
a per-stage mortality vector, and an RNG. Lowering returns an Ark world of
individuals, which we then run as a continuous-time jump process:

```{julia}
target = IBMStageTarget([10_000, 6_000, 4_000];
                        fecundity = [:reproduction],
                        death = [0.1, 0.1, 0.2],
                        rng = Random.Xoshiro(50))
world = lower(vnet, target)
res = ibm_run_stage!(world, (0.0, 4.0); dt = 0.01, saveat = 0.5, n_stages = 3)
res.counts[1]
```

## Agreement with the deterministic mean

The IBM is a pure-jump Markov process whose mean is the finite-state
generator $\dot n = G\,n$ assembled from the rates. The per-stage counts
track $\exp(Gt)\,n_0$:

```{julia}
G = [-0.6 0.0 0.6;       # = movements − (out-rate + death) on the diagonal + births
      0.5 -0.5 0.0;
      0.0 0.4 -0.2]
n0 = Float64.([10_000, 6_000, 4_000])
ibm_counts = reduce(hcat, [Float64.(c) for c in res.counts])'
det_counts = reduce(hcat, [exp(G .* t) * n0 for t in res.t])'

plot(res.t, det_counts; lw = 2, label = ["det. juv" "det. sub" "det. adult"])
plot!(res.t, ibm_counts; seriestype = :scatter,
      label = ["IBM juv" "IBM sub" "IBM adult"],
      xlabel = "time", ylabel = "count",
      title = "Individual-based lowering vs exp(Gt)·n₀")
```

## One specification, many realizations

The same `vnet` can be lowered along every route. For the discrete-state
backends these share the `fecundity` tagging:

| Target | Realization |
|---|---|
| `MPMTarget` / `DemographicMPMTarget` | discrete-time matrix model / its demographic draw |
| `FiniteStateDynamicsTarget` / `DemographicFiniteStateTarget` | continuous-time generator / its CTMC |
| `IBMStageTarget` | individual-based (Ark ECS) realization |

Lowering is just dispatch on the target, so switching realizations is a
one-line change:

```{julia}
typeof(lower(vnet, IBMStageTarget([100, 60, 40];
              fecundity = [:reproduction], death = [0.1, 0.1, 0.2])))
```

## Summary

- `IBMStageTarget(stages0; fecundity, death, rng)` lowers a stage-structured
  `ValuedProjectionNet` to an individual-based realization on Ark.jl,
  reusing the same `survival_fecundity_matrices` move-vs-birth split as the
  demographic targets.
- The lowered IBM reproduces the deterministic generator dynamics in the
  mean while simulating individual stochastic life histories.
- One categorical specification therefore spans deterministic, demographic,
  and individual-based realizations through a single `lower` interface.
